extraction.name: SeamlessAlign
extraction.description: A multimodal corpus of automatically aligned speech translations. It is described as the largest open dataset for multimodal translation to date, created through parallel data mining over raw audio and text corpora.
extraction.creator: Seamless Communication, Loïc Barrault, Yu-An Chung, Mariano Coria Meglioli, David Dale, Ning Dong, Paul-Ambroise Duquenne, Hady Elsahar, Hongyu Gong, Kevin Heffeman, John Hoffman, Christopher Klaiber, Pengwei Li, Daniel Licht, Jean Maillard, Alice Rakotoarison, Kaushik Ram Sadagopan, Guillaume Wenzek, Ethan Ye, Bapi Akula, Peng-Jen Chen, Naji El Hachem, Brian Ellis, Gabriel Mejia Gonzalez, Justin Haaheim, Prangthip Hansanti, Russ Howes, Bemie Huang, Min-Jae Hwang, Hirofumi Inaguma, Somya Jain, Elahe Kalbassi, Amanda Kallet, Ilia Kulikov, Janice Lam, Daniel Li, Xutai Ma, Ruslan Mavlyutov, Benjamin Peloquin, Mohamed Ramadan, Abinesh Ramakrishnan, Anna Sun, Kevin Tran, Tuan Tran, Igor Tufanov, Vish Vogeti, Carleigh Wood, Yilin Yang, Bokai Yu, Pierre Andrews, Can Balioglu, Marta R. Costa-jussà, Onur Celebi, Maha Elbayad, Cynthia Gao, Francisco Guzmán, Justine Kao, Ann Lee, Alexandre Mourachko, Juan Pino, Sravya Popuri, Christophe Ropers, Safiyyah Saleem, Holger Schwenk, Paden Tomasello, Changhan Wang, Jeff Wang, Skyler Wang
extraction.rai:dataCollection: We started with 4 million hours of raw audio from a publicly available repository of crawled web data, deduplicated audio file URLs, downloaded the audio files, resampled them at 16KHz, filtered out non-speech data with an audio event detection model, split audio into shorter overlapping segments with VAD, applied speech language identification, and mined translation pairs by projecting speech and text corpora into a common embedding space. On the text side, we relied entirely on the same dataset deployed in NLLB.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: For evaluation data, languages may not have recordings for all 350 sentences and not all three speaker recordings may be present; the paper also filtered out audio longer than 30 seconds.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: 4 million hours of raw audio from a publicly available repository of crawled web data, plus the same sentence-segmented text dataset drawn from NLLB.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: XSTS annotation and calibration process: during annotation, 3 annotators examined each source-target audio pair (or audio-text pair) and evaluated the item for semantic similarity using the XSTS protocol. Prior to annotating, all annotators went through monolingual English practice evaluations with score justifications. More than 3 (up to 30) annotators were used per language pair; each sentence pair was shown to 3 annotators assigned essentially randomly, with calibration set items intermixed. If the 3 annotators disagreed by 2 or more score values, 2 additional annotators evaluated the item again. The median score over annotators was taken. For MOS, a standard Mean Opinion Score protocol was used to evaluate naturalness, quality of sound, and clarity of speech.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Calibration and robustness checks were used: calibration set items were included, language-level scores were calibrated using the mean score on the calibration set, and the moderated calibration methodology was applied. The calibration process was found to reduce language-level annotator biases and improve correlation with automatic metrics. Annotator crews out of calibration could be identified and excluded or retrained.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: 3 annotators per item initially; 5 annotators for items with disagreement of 2 or more score values
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Monolingual English annotators for practice evaluations; no other demographics reported.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The paper reports added toxicity and gender bias in model outputs. It notes that SeamlessM4T "overgeneralizes to masculine forms when translating from neutral terms (with an average preference of ∼10%)" and that different languages show different toxicity distributions across demographic axes, with some languages' toxicity concentrated in particular axes.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The paper states that toxicity and gender imbalance detection rely on string-matching/word-list methods with known limitations: they can over-detect context-dependent terms, depend on precise tokenization, and ASR-before-matching can cause false negatives, especially for eng–X directions. It also says the gender-bias analysis uses a limited set of 30 nouns and may not generalize to other noun sets.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The paper says the work could improve accessibility and world-readiness by enabling multilingual speech translation, helping people communicate and learn in low-proficiency languages. It also frames the system as a step toward safer deployment by evaluating toxicity and bias and motivating mitigation efforts.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The paper discusses demographic attributes used in bias/toxicity analysis, including gender, age, race/ethnicity, religion, sexual orientation, socioeconomic class, nationality, cultural characteristics, body type, and political ideologies.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset/model outputs are used for evaluation of S2TT, S2ST, ASR, T2TT, and zero-shot T2ST. The paper also says the released models, inference code, and fine-tuning recipes are intended for the community, and that the tools can be used to create aligned speech data.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: For mining purposes, we followed an over-segmentation approach: used a Voice Activity Detection (VAD) model to split audio files into shorter segments, created several possible overlapping splits of each segment, and left the choice of the optimal split to the mining algorithm.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Text data used the same sources, cleaning, and filtering steps as NLLB. Audio data were deduplicated by URL, downloaded, resampled at 16 kHz, filtered to remove non-speech with an audio event detection model, and audio longer than 30 seconds was filtered out.
